_comment: SYNTHETIC DOCUMENTATION FIXTURE. Trench T905, its personnel, its
coordinates, its elevations and its finds are invented. Nothing here is
archaeological evidence and none of it may be used for interpretation.
It is not invented freely, though. Real excavation records do not arrive
clean, and an example built from tidy numbers teaches the wrong lesson:
it shows the happy path and hides every refusal. So T905 is modelled on
the SHAPE of a real season's paperwork -- the same kinds of gap,
disagreement, transcription slip and unrecorded value -- while carrying
none of its content. Every defect below is deliberate and documented.
The one that matters most is in `corners`: the northeast corner has no
opening elevation, so one wall cannot be registered and the build refuses

datumNail.label: T905 2025, nail in a tree by the southwest corner (corrected value)

corners.record: invented, in the form of a season Geospatial Spreadsheet
note: A real sheet stores these already signed, as 'NW: 150/-20' rather
than '150E/20S', because the site's cardinal-inversion rule (South
and West negative) is applied before the number reaches the sheet.
The labels here are in the trench-book spelling so that the
conversion is visible; see tests/fixtures/geospatial-sample.csv for
the signed form.

elevations.record: invented, in the form of a trench book's opening elevations
note: Three of the four corners only. The NE corner at 155E/20S has NO
opening elevation and is absent here rather than filled in.
The reason is the one that produces this gap in practice: T905's
northeastern meters fall inside a trench excavated in a previous
season and backfilled. Locus 1, the opening topsoil, covers only the
ground that was not dug before, so the opening elevation list stops
at 151E/20S -- the eastern limit of Locus 1 -- and the trench's own
northeast corner never gets an opening reading at all.
That corner does receive an elevation eventually, as Locus 3's NE3 at
23.96 mAE, but that is a floor surface measured 15 days and two loci
later. It is not the trench's opening surface and is not used here.
The SW corner's 24.70 mAE is NOT natural relief. It is the crest of a
spoil heap left by an earlier season, 0.52 m deep, which was removed
as part of Locus 1.

datumNail.record: invented, in the form of a trench book's Trench Layout section
note: First shot at 25.73 mAE at the start of the season.
CORRECTED mid-season: the datum points established at the start of the
season were found to be 0.50 m high because of a transit error. They
were reshot and every point recorded before the correction was
adjusted. T905's datum is 25.23 mAE.
25.23 is the value used here, and every elevation in this fixture and
in t905-2025-loci and t905-2025-special-finds is on the corrected
scale. See _known_problems for how that can be checked rather than
taken on trust.
T905 sits on the Piano del Tesoro, so the hill grid rather than
Vescovado di Murlo. The two origins are about 1.5 million metres
apart once projected, so a config that names neither is not merely
untidy.
Named from the corner labels: two corners sharing a cardinal letter
name the wall between them, so NW to NE is the north wall. All four
sides come out 5.00 m, matching the recorded 5 m by 5 m trench.

_known_problems: THE EAST WALL CANNOT BE REGISTERED. Its origin corner is NE, which has no
opening elevation, so its surfaceZ is null and the build refuses it. The
other three walls register from surveyed values with no placeholders.
This is the documented refusal working correctly, and it is the reason
this fixture exists: a trench that registers cleanly cannot demonstrate
it.
THE TWO SEASONS' BASELINES DISAGREE BY 30 cm. While triangulating the
corners the team found that a point projected as 156E from the previous
season's baseline lies 30 cm west of the same label projected from this
season's. They chose to keep the earlier baseline so that the coordinates
of the structure recorded then would still line up. Every coordinate here
is therefore on the earlier baseline, deliberately, and is offset about
0.30 m from anything shot against the newer one. Combining this trench
with one that used the newer baseline means reconciling that first.
THE DATUM NAIL'S PLAN POSITION IS RECORDED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS. The
Trench Layout section puts it on a tree outside the southwest corner; a
daily entry puts the same tree in the centre of the trench; the locus
descriptions refer to 'the tree in the southwest'. Its ELEVATION is
consistent everywhere. Its easting and northing are recorded nowhere, so
this fixture gives it none.
THE DAY-1 CLOSING ELEVATION REPEATS THE OPENING ONE AT SW. Both read
24.70 mAE, on a day spent lowering the spoil heap in exactly that corner.
The next day's closing reads 24.26 mAE there. The day-1 closing figure
looks carried over rather than freshly measured, so only the opening set
is used here.
THE ELEVATIONS ARE ON THE CORRECTED (25.23) SCALE, and the sequence shows
it rather than the record merely asserting it. The locus closed the day
before the datum was reshot and the locus opened the day after are
continuous: one closes at 23.87-24.02 mAE and the next opens at
23.87-23.99 mAE at points inside it. A 0.50 m step at that boundary would
be unmistakable, and there is none. That is what a retrospectively
corrected elevation series looks like, and it is worth checking for
before trusting one.
